To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified VH replacement in human B cells that lacks AID-mediated processing.

we have identified a novel form of VH replacement in human preimmune B cells, that VH replacement is mediated by an activation-induced cytidene deamination (AID)-independent mechanism, and that the mechanism involves RAG-mediated cleavages at cryptic RSS embedded within the VH4 gene family.

1) VH replacement occurs in preimmune human fetal and adult B cells; 2) VH replacement in preimmune B cells is mediated through a cryptic hepta-13 nonamer recombination signal sequence in VH genes, and; 3) VH replacement in B cells is independent of activation-induced cytidie deaminase (AICDA).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular basis of BCR editing in the human B cell repertoire and suggests a mechanism that is distinct from the AICDA-dependent mechanism that is believed to contribute to Ig somatic hypermutation.
how the human immune system generates a functional repertoire of B cells that can respond to a diverse array of foreign Ags.
the development of the human Ig repertoire.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VH replacement in humans is a rare phenomenon, which is mediated by a RAG-dependent mechanism that is independent of AICDA.
VH4 replacement is not a significant mechanism in the generation of the human Ig repertoire.
AICDA is not required for VH replacement in preimmune B cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VH4 cSSR is a better substrate than the VH3 and VH5 cSSR, but it is still inefficient and requires a high level of RAG1 expression.
the VH4 cRS is a weak RAG substrate in vivo, and that VH4 replacement is a rare but significant contributor to the normal human Ig repertoire.
VH4 replacement is an important process for generating diversity in preimmune human IgH repertoire.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VH4 cRS is an active substrate for RAG-mediated cleavages in preimmune B cells.
VH4 replacement occurs in preimmune human fetal and adult B cells and is mediated by an inefficient but selective RGS-mediated cleavage at the VH4 cRS.
VH replacement in human B cells is not dependent on AICDA.
